name: run_guest_cmd
prose: Precondition: vcpu, gic_fd, inject_args and test_args point to valid objects, and the process is aborted unless inject_args->first_intid < UINT_MAX - inject_args->num or inject_args->num == 1. Postcondition: depending on inject_args->cmd the function does nothing for any other command, or for KVM_INJECT_EDGE_IRQ_LINE calls kvm_irq_line_check(vm, i, 1, test_args, expect_failure) then kvm_irq_line_check(vm, i, 0, test_args, expect_failure) for each i in [intid, intid+num) using 64-bit loop arithmetic, for KVM_SET_IRQ_LINE calls kvm_irq_line_check(vm, i, level, test_args, expect_failure) for each such i, for KVM_SET_IRQ_LINE_HIGH calls kvm_irq_line_check(vm, i, 1, test_args, expect_failure) for each such i, for KVM_SET_LEVEL_INFO_HIGH calls kvm_irq_set_level_info_check(gic_fd, i, 1, expect_failure) for each such i, for KVM_INJECT_IRQFD calls kvm_routing_and_irqfd_check(vm, intid, num, test_args->kvm_max_routes, expect_failure) exactly once, and for KVM_WRITE_ISPENDR and KVM_WRITE_ISACTIVER loops with 32-bit i from intid while i < (uint32_t)(intid + num), so it makes no calls when intid + num overflows uint32_t (only possible under the precondition when num == 1 and intid == UINT_MAX) and otherwise calls kvm_irq_write_ispendr_check(gic_fd, i, vcpu, expect_failure) or kvm_irq_write_isactiver(gic_fd, i, vcpu) for each i in [intid, intid+num); the process is aborted if the initial assert or any assertion in a called helper fails, and the function itself takes no locks and allocates nothing directly, but on the KVM_INJECT_IRQFD path its helper kvm_routing_and_irqfd_check builds a GSI routing table and creates one eventfd per interrupt (the eventfds are closed before it returns).
note: reviewer (round15) right: the 'allocates no memory' claim was false for the KVM_INJECT_IRQFD path (vgic_irq.c:597-640, 552-580); rounds 1/2 points (32-bit ISPENDR/ISACTIVER loop overflow at intid=UINT_MAX, IRQFD helper called once) were already in the prose. Prose re-read against vgic_irq.c:648-705.

name: run_test
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a valid vCPU running the guest code of guest_print_test, whose ucalls are UCALL_PRINTF (formatted output) and UCALL_ABORT (an intentional guest assert) followed by UCALL_DONE; expected_printf and expected_assert are NUL-terminated strings. Postcondition (run_test, guest_print_test.c:125-156): it loops: runs the vCPU with do_vcpu_run (KVM_RUN retried on EINTR, any other error fails TEST_ASSERT), asserts that the exit reason is UCALL_EXIT_REASON, and handles the ucall: UCALL_PRINTF requires uc.buffer to equal expected_printf exactly (strcmp), UCALL_ABORT requires uc.buffer to be at least as long as expected_assert and to end with it (ucall_abort compares only that trailing substring), UCALL_DONE makes the function return, and any other ucall, including UCALL_SYNC, fails the test with TEST_FAIL. A failed TEST_ASSERT or TEST_FAIL terminates the test instead of returning. The function returns void.
note: reviewer (round15) right: UCALL_SYNC is not accepted, it hits TEST_FAIL('Unknown args_type', guest_print_test.c:139-141), so it cannot be listed as an expected ucall; round-0 reviewer's suffix-only point (ucall_abort, 95-106) was already in the prose.

name: vm_compute_max_gfn
prose: Precondition: vm points to an initialized struct kvm_vm whose page_shift and pa_bits are set. Postcondition (vm_compute_max_gfn, processor.c:1251-1300; slice cut the head, 'max_gfn' is a local variable): it takes the guest MAXPHYADDR from the KVM CPU property X86_PROPERTY_GUEST_MAX_PHY_ADDR (falling back to vm->pa_bits when that is 0), asserts that it is not greater than vm->pa_bits (TEST_ASSERT aborts otherwise), and computes max_gfn = (1ULL << (guest_maxphyaddr - vm->page_shift)) - 1. It returns max_gfn if the host CPU is not AMD or if vm->pa_bits < 40. Otherwise it computes ht_gfn, the first frame of the HyperTransport hole, with num_ht_pages = 12 << (30 - vm->page_shift) (a local constant, the pages of 12 GiB): (1 << 28) - num_ht_pages for a CPU family below 0x17 or when X86_PROPERTY_MAX_PHY_ADDR is not enumerated; otherwise max_pfn - num_ht_pages, where max_pfn = (1ULL << (maxphyaddr - vm->page_shift)) - 1 with maxphyaddr from X86_PROPERTY_MAX_PHY_ADDR, right-shifted by X86_PROPERTY_PHYS_ADDR_REDUCTION when that property is enumerated. It returns min(max_gfn, ht_gfn - 1). It reads CPU properties only and has no side effects.
note: slice cut the head; real function vm_compute_max_gfn. Old prose called num_ht_pages a positive global; it is a local constant 12 << (30 - page_shift) (processor.c:1253), and the guest_maxphyaddr source/assert were omitted.

name: rotate
prose: Precondition: size is 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 (any other value makes cut_to_size call GUEST_FAIL); amount may be any int, including a negative one. Postcondition (rotate, memop.c:511-520; pure apart from that failure): let bits = size * 8 and amount' = (amount + bits) % bits, computed in unsigned arithmetic (since bits is a power of two dividing 2^32, this is amount reduced into [0, bits) for every int amount, so a negative amount rotates the other way). It masks val to its low bits with cut_to_size. If amount' is 0 it returns that masked value. Otherwise it returns (val << (bits - amount')) | (val >> amount') as a 128-bit value; for size < 16 the left-shifted part can set bits at or above position size * 8, so the result is not truncated back to size * 8 bits (only for size 16 is it exactly a rotate right of the whole value).
note: reviewer (round15) right on both points: callers pass negative amounts (memop.c:567-574) and the result is not masked to size*8 bits for size < 16 (line 519); round-2 reviewer's claim that negatives are misnormalized is wrong because bits is always a power of two dividing 2^32.

name: guest_error_key
prose: Precondition: runs as s390 KVM guest code with no parameters (the host drives it by running the vCPU and handling syncs). Postcondition (guest_error_key, memop.c:768-775; returns void): it first issues GUEST_SYNC(STAGE_INITED), which exits to the host; when resumed it sets the storage key 0x18 on the first page of the global buffer mem1 and the key 0x98 on the rest of mem1 (set_storage_key_range), then issues GUEST_SYNC(STAGE_SKEYS_SET) and GUEST_SYNC(STAGE_IDLED), after which it returns to its caller (whether the host ever resumes the guest after the last sync is up to the host).
note: reviewer (round15) right: the function does return after the last GUEST_SYNC (memop.c:770-775); round-0 reviewer's ordering point (STAGE_INITED is emitted before the keys are set) was already correct in the old prose.

name: TEST_F(uc_kvm, uc_set_gsi_routing)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(uc_kvm, uc_set_gsi_routing) (ucontrol_test.c:779-796); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: self->vm_fd is an open KVM VM file descriptor. Postcondition: it creates a routing table with kvm_gsi_routing_create(), stores in entry 0 a KVM_IRQ_ROUTING_S390_ADAPTER entry for gsi 1 with ind_addr 0 and sets nr to 1, calls the KVM_SET_GSI_ROUTING ioctl on self->vm_fd, and asserts (ASSERT_EQ, which stops the test on failure) that it returned -1 and that errno is EINVAL. The routing table is not freed by the test.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); prose re-read against ucontrol_test.c:779-796; added that the routing table is not freed. Named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function).

name: guest_code
prose: RISC-V variant of guest_code(int cpu) (steal_time.c:243-267, inside the #elif defined(__riscv) block; the slice starts earlier and ends in the middle of it). Precondition: runs as KVM guest code on vCPU number cpu, with st_gva[cpu] and st_gpa[cpu] already synchronized by the host and the SBI STA extension available. Postcondition: it probes the SBI STA extension and requires (GUEST_ASSERT) that it is present with value 1, registers the shared steal-time memory st_gpa[cpu] with sta_set_shmem (which asserts a zero SBI return value and error), and issues GUEST_SYNC(0). After the host resumes it, it asserts that the steal-time record is consistent (even sequence, zero flags, zero preempted flag), saves st->steal in guest_stolen_time[cpu], reads the sequence number, re-checks the record and issues GUEST_SYNC(1). After the second resume it re-checks the record, asserts that the sequence number has increased, saves st->steal again, re-checks the record, and ends with GUEST_DONE(). Any failing GUEST_ASSERT aborts the guest with a failure report.
note: slice cut the tail; the dropped item had no prose; written from the RISC-V guest_code at steal_time.c:243-267 (the file has three guest_code variants: x86 at 42, arm64 at 131, riscv at 243).

name: main
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the test's command line (unused); the host supports XFD, XSAVE and the AMX tile features, otherwise TEST_REQUIRE skips the test. Postcondition (main, amx_test.c:222-335; slice cut the head, 'amx_test_main' is not a function name): it requests permission for XFEATURE_MASK_XTILE_DATA, checks the required CPU features, creates a VM with one vCPU running guest_code (so, unlike the old prose, main itself creates the VM), reads the maximum XSAVE size (TEST_ASSERT it is enumerated), saves the initial registers, installs the #NM exception handler, allocates and fills the AMX config page, a 2-page tile data area with a random nonzero byte pattern and the XSAVE area, and passes the three addresses to the vCPU as arguments. It then loops: it runs the vCPU, requires a KVM_EXIT_IO exit (TEST_ASSERT), and handles the ucall: UCALL_ABORT reports the guest assertion and does not continue; UCALL_SYNC, depending on the flags in the sync argument, saves the vCPU state (tile state), compares tile register 0 of the saved XSAVE data with the tile data page (TEST_ASSERT on mismatch), restores the saved XSAVE state with KVM_SET_XSAVE, and/or saves the whole vCPU state, releases the VM, recreates a VM with one vCPU, loads the state and asserts that the registers equal those saved; UCALL_DONE leaves the loop; any other ucall fails with TEST_FAIL. After the loop it frees the VM with kvm_vm_free and main returns (0, the end of main has no return statement).
note: slice cut the head; real function main. Reviewer (round15) right: the VM is created inside main (amx_test.c:248), not by the caller as the old precondition said.

name: l2_guest_code
prose: Precondition: runs as the L2 guest, entered by L1 with vmlaunch/vmresume under an enlightened VMCS. When L2 starts, L1 has not yet enabled MSR-bitmap interception: L1 sets CPU_BASED_USE_MSR_BITMAPS and the MSR_FS_BASE intercept bit only after handling L2's first vmcall, and sets the MSR_GS_BASE intercept bit later (after the second vmcall). Postcondition (l2_guest_code, hyperv_evmcs.c:42-76; returns void): it issues GUEST_SYNC(7), GUEST_SYNC(8) and GUEST_SYNC(9) (the last forces an exit to L1 on restore), then a vmcall; after L1 has enabled the FS_BASE intercept it reads MSR_FS_BASE twice (intercepted) and MSR_GS_BASE (not intercepted at that point), issues another vmcall, and after L1 has changed the bitmap reads MSR_GS_BASE again (intercepted). It then issues a fast HVCALL_FLUSH_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_SPACE hypercall (flush all address spaces and processors) through hyperv_hypercall, reads MSR_FS_BASE, issues the same hypercall through __hyperv_hypercall (status not checked, because L1 does not preserve RAX after the synthetic vmexit), and finishes with a vmcall to L1 that L1 does not resume.
note: reviewer (round15) right: L1 installs the FS_BASE intercept after L2's first vmcall (hyperv_evmcs.c:138-145), not before L2 starts, and enables GS_BASE interception later (156-161); round-0 reviewer's point is the same and is covered. The vmcall at the end is not resumed (L1 goes on to GUEST_SYNC(11)).

name: guest_test_hcalls_access
prose: Precondition: the caller (main) has checked with TEST_REQUIRE that KVM_CAP_HYPERV_ENFORCE_CPUID is available; the function takes no arguments and returns void. Postcondition (guest_test_hcalls_access, hyperv_features.c:519-684): it loops over stages 0 to 21. For stages 0 to 20 it creates a fresh VM with one vCPU running guest_hcall, allocates a zeroed 2-page hypercall input/output area and a zeroed one-page struct hcall_data that it passes to the guest, enables KVM_CAP_HYPERV_ENFORCE_CPUID, and sets the vCPU CPUID: at stage 0 it resets the Hyper-V CPUID and allocates prev_cpuid (a heap copy that is never freed), at later stages it starts from prev_cpuid, so features granted by earlier stages stay enabled. Each stage then sets hcall->control to a hypercall code and enables the Hyper-V feature bit that is to be tested; for most stages it also sets hcall->expect to the status the guest should see (access denied, invalid code or input, success, and so on), while stage 17 instead sets hcall->ud_expected = true (a fast XMM hypercall without the XMM-input feature must raise #UD) and stage 18, after enabling that feature, clears ud_expected and expects HV_STATUS_SUCCESS. It then applies the CPUID, saves it into prev_cpuid, runs the vCPU, asserts a KVM_EXIT_IO exit and examines the ucall: UCALL_DONE moves to the next stage after freeing the VM; UCALL_ABORT reports the guest assertion (REPORT_GUEST_ASSERT fails the test) and the source then returns; any other ucall fails the test with TEST_FAIL and returns. At stage 21 it frees the VM and returns without running any hypercall.
note: reviewer (round15) right: stage 17 sets hcall->ud_expected (a #UD expectation), not hcall->expect (hyperv_features.c:636-646); the old prose only mentioned the expected status. Round-0 reviewer's stage-21 point (no hypercall is run) was already in the old prose.

name: guest_code
prose: Precondition: runs as KVM guest code; arg is NULL or the address of the nested-virtualization data allocated by the host (struct svm_test_data on SVM hosts, struct vmx_pages on VMX hosts); the host services the SYNC_PORT I/O exits (the guest reports a stage by an 'in' from port 0xe) and injects SMIs for stages 8 and 10. Postcondition (guest_code, smm_test.c:66-114; returns void): it reads MSR_IA32_APICBASE, reports stage 1, sets the x2APIC enable bit in that MSR, reports stage 2, and sends itself an SMI (self_smi); the SMI handler in SMRAM reports the fixed stage SMRAM_STAGE (0xfe) on the host's third exit and resumes (rsm). It then reports stage 4. If arg is non-NULL it sets up a nested guest (generic_svm_setup, or prepare_for_vmx_operation, load_vmcs and prepare_vmcs under GUEST_ASSERT) running l2_guest_code, reports stage 5, sends a second self-SMI (reported as SMRAM_STAGE), reports stage 7, runs the L2 guest twice (run_guest twice on SVM, vmlaunch then vmresume on VMX; the stages reported while L2 runs, 8 to 11, are replaced on the host side by SMRAM_STAGE reports from injected SMIs), and reports stage 12. In every case it ends by reporting DONE (0xff); with arg NULL stages 5, 7 and 12 and the second self-SMI are skipped.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the second self_smi (smm_test.c:97) and the SMRAM_STAGE reports from the SMI handler (lines 39-43, which the host sees in place of stages 3 and 6) were omitted; round-0 reviewer's NULL-arg point was already covered by the old prose.

name: vmx_l2_guest_code
prose: Precondition: the function is entered as the L2 guest under VMX non-root operation with a shadow VMCS current (L1 sets that shadow VMCS up only after the first vmcall), and no particular GUEST_RIP value is required at entry. Postcondition: it syncs stages 6, 10, 11 and 12; after the first vmcall it asserts GUEST_RIP == 0xc0ffee (both before and after sync 10), writes GUEST_RIP = 0xc0fffee with vmwrite (asserting the write succeeds) and asserts GUEST_RIP == 0xc0fffee, writes GUEST_RIP = 0xc0ffffee with vmwrite (asserting the write succeeds) without reading it back, and finally exits to L1 via vmcall with GUEST_RIP == 0xc0ffffee; any failed GUEST_ASSERT aborts the guest.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against state_test.c:54-73: the L2 stage list, the precondition (shadow VMCS with GUEST_RIP 0xc0ffee set up by L1 only after the first vmcall), the two vmwrite asserts and the absence of a read-back after the second write all match; prose kept. Round-0/2 reviewers' points are already reflected.

name: vmx_l1_guest_code
prose: Precondition: runs as L1 guest code; vmx_pages points to a struct vmx_pages set up by the host with a nonzero vmcs_gpa (asserted at entry; shadow_vmcs_gpa is used later but not checked). Postcondition (vmx_l1_guest_code, state_test.c:75-136; returns void): it calls prepare_for_vmx_operation (so VMX need not be enabled beforehand), reports stage 3, loads the VMCS and checks vmptrstz() equals vmcs_gpa, reports stage 4, prepares the VMCS to run vmx_l2_guest_code, reports stage 5 and launches L2, asserting that the launch succeeds and that the exit reason is EXIT_REASON_VMCALL. It then asserts that a second vmlaunch fails (the launched state is preserved), that vmresume succeeds with exit reason VMCALL, reports stage 7 and resumes L2 again (success and VMCALL asserted). It advances GUEST_RIP by 3 and enables shadow-VMCS use with unchecked vmwrite calls to SECONDARY_VM_EXEC_CONTROL and VMCS_LINK_POINTER, makes the shadow VMCS current with vmptrld (asserted to succeed), asserts that vmlaunch and vmresume both fail while the shadow VMCS is current, reports stage 8, writes GUEST_RIP = 0xc0ffee into it (vmwrite result unchecked), reports stage 9 and asserts it reads back as 0xc0ffee. It then makes the normal VMCS current again, resumes L2 (success and VMCALL exit asserted), makes the shadow VMCS current again and asserts that GUEST_RIP reads 0xc0ffffee, asserts that vmlaunch and vmresume fail, reports stage 13, asserts GUEST_RIP is still 0xc0ffffee, asserts that vmlaunch and vmresume fail again and returns. Any failed GUEST_ASSERT aborts the guest.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); rewritten from state_test.c:75-136: only vmcs_gpa is checked at entry (the old precondition also required shadow_vmcs_gpa), and the repeated vmlaunch/vmresume calls under GUEST_ASSERT are expected to fail while the shadow VMCS is current, which the old prose did not state; round-1/2 reviewers' points (prepare_for_vmx_operation is called inside; vmwrite results are unchecked) were already reflected.

name: l2_guest_code
prose: Precondition: runs as the L2 guest, entered by L1's vmlaunch; the VMX preemption timer is not yet enabled at that point: L1 handles L2's first vmcall, then turns on the pin-based timer control, sets the timer value and vmx_pt_rate, and resumes L2. Postcondition (l2_guest_code, vmx_preemption_timer_test.c:36-65; returns void in source but does not return in practice): it issues a vmcall to exit to L1; after L1 resumes it, it sets l2_vmx_pt_start to the TSC with its low vmx_pt_rate bits cleared, then loops loading l2_vmx_pt_finish with the raw rdtsc() value until the elapsed TSC (finish - start, shifted right by vmx_pt_rate) reaches PREEMPTION_TIMER_VALUE_THRESHOLD1. It then issues GUEST_SYNC(1) (a save/restore point for the host), sets l2_save_restore_done = 1 and loops forever loading l2_vmx_pt_finish with rdtsc() until the preemption timer fires and the CPU exits to L1; the function never reaches its end.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the timer is armed by L1 after L2's initial vmcall (vmx_preemption_timer_test.c:96-116), not before L2 entry, and the initial vmcall was omitted; round-0 reviewer's point that l2_vmx_pt_finish holds raw rdtsc values (not aligned ones) was already correct in the old prose.

name: guest_code
prose: Precondition: runs as guest code with the Xen shared_info mapped at SHINFO_VADDR and the runstate area at RUNSTATE_VADDR; a host VMM services each GUEST_SYNC (the sync argument names the next test stage) and performs the corresponding setup, so the guest's checks depend on what the host did before resuming it. Postcondition (guest_code, xen_shinfo_test.c:189-379; returns void): it enables interrupts and then works through the stages in order, each started by a GUEST_SYNC with the stage name: TEST_INJECT_VECTOR (followed by guest_wait_for_irq), the three host-set runstate stages (runnable, blocked, offline: each asserts the matching rs->time entry is nonzero and rs->state == 0), TEST_RUNSTATE_ADJUST and TEST_RUNSTATE_DATA and TEST_STEAL_TIME (asserts on rs->time[] and state_entry_time), TEST_EVTCHN_MASKED (then spins until the shared_info evtchn_pending[0] word is nonzero), TEST_EVTCHN_UNMASKED, TEST_EVTCHN_SLOWPATH and TEST_EVTCHN_SEND_IOCTL (each followed by guest_wait_for_irq), TEST_EVTCHN_HCALL, TEST_EVTCHN_HCALL_SLOWPATH and TEST_EVTCHN_HCALL_EVENTFD (each sends an event channel hypercall, ports 127, 127 and 197, then waits for the irq), TEST_TIMER_SETUP (arms a timer 100 ms ahead with set_timer_op), TEST_TIMER_WAIT and TEST_TIMER_RESTORE (wait for the irq), TEST_POLL_READY, TEST_POLL_TIMEOUT and TEST_POLL_MASKED (each issues a SCHEDOP_poll hypercall and does not wait for an irq), TEST_POLL_WAKE and SET_VCPU_INFO syncs followed by a SCHEDOP_poll on the next port and a guest_wait_for_irq, TEST_TIMER_PAST and TEST_LOCKING_SEND_RACE (each followed by guest_wait_for_irq), and TEST_LOCKING_POLL_RACE followed by a loop of up to 100 SCHEDOP_poll hypercalls until the interrupt flag guest_saw_irq is set, issuing GUEST_SYNC(TEST_LOCKING_POLL_TIMEOUT) and retrying when it was not. Failed GUEST_ASSERTs abort the guest. After clearing guest_saw_irq it issues GUEST_SYNC(TEST_DONE) and returns.
note: reviewer (round15) right: guest_wait_for_irq is called after the SCHEDOP_poll that follows TEST_POLL_WAKE/SET_VCPU_INFO (xen_shinfo_test.c:321-333), so 'only at the stages that expect an interrupt, not at the poll stages' was too loose; round-0 reviewer's point (several poll stages advance without waiting) is covered. Also corrected: the function returns after the final GUEST_SYNC(TEST_DONE) instead of never returning.

name: test_relative_path
prose: Precondition: the layout1 fixture directory tree under TMP_DIR exists (dir_s1d2, dir_s2d2 and their subdirectories); rel is REL_OPEN, REL_CHDIR, REL_CHROOT_ONLY or REL_CHROOT_CHDIR (any other value fails ASSERT_TRUE(false) and returns). Postcondition (test_relative_path, fs_test.c:1903-2018; returns void): it creates its own first-layer ruleset (read-only access on TMP_DIR), enforces it and closes it; it then creates a second-layer ruleset (read-only on dir_s1d2 and dir_s2d2), changes the working directory to dir_s2d2 for REL_CHROOT_ONLY or to dir_s1d2 for REL_CHROOT_CHDIR (not for the other two), raises CAP_SYS_CHROOT with set_cap and enforces the second ruleset. According to rel it then opens dir_s1d2 as a directory fd (REL_OPEN), changes directory to dir_s1d2 (REL_CHDIR), chroots to ../../s1d1/s1d2 (REL_CHROOT_ONLY) or to '.' (REL_CHROOT_CHDIR). It asserts that opening '..' relative to the chosen directory gives EACCES (0 for REL_CHROOT_CHDIR) and '.' and the allowed subdirectory succeed; for the chroot modes it asserts that '/..', '/', '/f1' and '/s1d3' open; for the other three modes it asserts that ../../s1d1 and ../../s2d1 are denied with EACCES while the allowed directories below them open. Any failed ASSERT stops the test. At the end it closes the directory fd for REL_OPEN only, and closes the second ruleset fd. The working directory stays changed for REL_CHDIR, REL_CHROOT_ONLY and REL_CHROOT_CHDIR (not for REL_OPEN), the root directory stays changed for the chroot modes, and CAP_SYS_CHROOT is not dropped.
note: reviewer (round15) right: for REL_OPEN the working directory is never changed (fs_test.c:1958-1960); round-0 reviewer's point that the function builds its own rulesets (no precondition on layers) was already right in the prose.

name: TEST_F_FORK(layout1_bind, path_disconnected)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F_FORK(layout1_bind, path_disconnected) (fs_test.c:5041-5133; the test runs in a forked child); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: the layout1_bind hierarchy exists and no ruleset is enforced yet. Postcondition: it creates three rulesets before touching the files (layer 1 allows all accesses on TMP_DIR, layer 2 READ_FILE on file1_s1d3, layer 3 READ_FILE on dir_s1d2; each creation is asserted with ASSERT_LE), enforces layer 1 and closes it, and opens an O_PATH | O_CLOEXEC descriptor on bind_dir_s1d3 (never closed by the test). Through that descriptor it expects file1_name and file2_name to open read-only and '..' to open as a directory (EXPECT_EQ), renames dir_s1d3 to dir_s4d1 (ASSERT_EQ 0), expects the two files to still open through the descriptor and '..' now to fail with ENOENT, enforces and closes layer 2 and expects file1_s4d1 to open, file1_name through the descriptor to open and file2_name through it to fail with EACCES, then enforces and closes layer 3 and expects file1_s4d1 to fail with EACCES, file1_name through the descriptor to still open and file2_name to fail with EACCES. Only the ruleset creations and the rename abort the test on failure; the file-open checks are EXPECT_* and just record failures.
note: reviewer (round15) right: most checks are EXPECT_EQ (fs_test.c:5087-5132) so failures do not abort, contrary to the old prose; only the ASSERT_LE ruleset checks and the rename (5092) abort. Named by the TEST_F_FORK invocation.

name: TEST_F_FORK(layout1_bind, path_disconnected_rename)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F_FORK(layout1_bind, path_disconnected_rename) (fs_test.c:5140-5304; the test runs in a forked child); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: the layout1_bind hierarchy exists and no ruleset is enforced. Postcondition: it creates dir_s4d1 (ASSERT_EQ 0) and two rulesets: layer 1 grants REFER, MAKE_DIR, REMOVE_DIR, MAKE_REG, REMOVE_FILE and READ_FILE on dir_s1d2 and on dir_s4d1, layer 2 handles only READ_FILE and grants it on dir_s1d2. It enforces and closes layer 1, opens an O_PATH descriptor on bind_dir_s1d3 (never closed), expects file1 to open through it and '..' to fail with EACCES, renames dir_s1d3 to dir_s4d2 (ASSERT_EQ 0) and expects '..' to fail with ENOENT. In a forked child it enforces layer 2 and expects file1 through the descriptor to open and file1_s4d2 to fail with EACCES, and expects renaming dir_s4d2 back to dir_s1d3 and a renameat through the descriptor to fail with -1/EXDEV; the parent waits and expects the child to exit normally with EXIT_SUCCESS (the child exits with _metadata->exit_code). The parent renames the directory back (ASSERT_EQ 0) and a second forked child enforces layer 2 and expects file1 through the descriptor and file1_s1d3 to open. The parent then renames the directory back to dir_s4d2, renames file1 to file2 within the disconnected directory through the descriptor, renames file2 out to file1_s2d2 and back in through the descriptor (each asserted with ASSERT_EQ 0, with EXPECT checks that the files open), reconnects the directory (rename dir_s4d2 to dir_s1d3, asserted), enforces layer 2 in the parent, and expects file1 through the descriptor and file1_s1d3 to open. It opens a socket (ASSERT_LE) and expects, as EXPECT_EQ checks that only record failures, a bind with an address length one byte short to return -EINVAL and a bind to AF_UNSPEC/INADDR_ANY to return 0 for AF_INET, -EAFNOSUPPORT for AF_INET6 and -EINVAL for any other domain (this first bind is allowed by the rule, so it does not depend on whether the protocol is restricted), then closes the socket. When sandboxed it enforces a second ruleset handling bind with no rule (bind denied), opens a fresh socket, and expects the same AF_UNSPEC/INADDR_ANY bind to return -EACCES for AF_INET when the protocol is restricted and 0 when it is not, -EAFNOSUPPORT for AF_INET6 and -EINVAL otherwise, then closes it. Finally, with a third fresh socket, it expects a bind with AF_UNSPEC and the loopback address to return -EAFNOSUPPORT for AF_INET and AF_INET6 and -EINVAL otherwise, and closes it.

name: main
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the command line: argv[1] is the path of a file on the fuse_mnt mount (a FUSE file whose read is delayed by 1 s) and the optional argv[2] is 'hugetlbfs'. Postcondition (main, fuse_test.c:228-331; slice cut the head): it prints a message and calls abort() if argc < 2, if argv[2] is given and is not 'hugetlbfs', or (for 'hugetlbfs') if the default huge page size cannot be determined; with 'hugetlbfs' it sets the memfd size to twice the huge page size. It allocates a zero-filled comparison buffer with calloc (the result is not checked), opens argv[1] read-only (abort() on failure), creates a sealable memfd of that size and maps it shared (the mfd_assert_* helpers abort on failure), and starts a sealing thread that, after 200 ms, unmaps the mapping and tries to add F_SEAL_WRITE (expecting it to fail while the FUSE read is pending and succeed after one more second). It then read()s the FUSE file into the memfd mapping, aborting if read fails or returns 0, records whether F_SEAL_WRITE was already set, waits for the sealing thread and asserts that the memfd has F_SEAL_WRITE. It maps the memfd privately and aborts if the memfd was sealed during the read but its data is not all zero, or if it was not sealed but its data is all zero. Otherwise it closes the memfd and the file descriptor, prints 'fuse: DONE', frees the comparison buffer and returns 0. Every checked failure ends in abort(); the only unchecked failure is the calloc result.
note: slice cut the head. Reviewer (round15) right: the calloc result is not checked (fuse_test.c:258), so not every failure path aborts; the rest of the old prose re-read against fuse_test.c:228-331 and kept in substance.

name: TEST_F(hmm, anon_teardown)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(hmm, anon_teardown) (hmm-tests.c:1413-1469); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: self->fd is open on the dmirror device and self->page_size and page_shift are set. Postcondition: it computes npages from HMM_BUFFER_SIZE and then repeats NTIMES times: it allocates an hmm_buffer and its mirror with malloc (ASSERT_NE NULL), maps npages anonymous private pages and fills them with ptr[i] == i + c (c is the iteration number), and only then creates a thread running unmap_buffer, which sleeps for a pseudo-random time (below 32 ms), unmaps the second half of the buffer and sets buffer->ptr to NULL. Concurrently it issues HMM_DMIRROR_READ on the buffer; if that returns 0 it asserts that cpages equals npages, faults equals 1 and every mirror entry equals i + c, and if it returns nonzero it makes no further checks. In both cases it joins the thread and frees the buffer and mirror with hmm_buffer_free. Failures of the ASSERT_* checks stop the test.

name: TEST_F(hmm, exclusive)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(hmm, exclusive) (hmm-tests.c:1784-1836); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: the fixture is initialized (self->fd open on the dmirror device, page_size and page_shift set) and the dmirror device supports exclusive access. Postcondition: it allocates an hmm_buffer and its mirror (ASSERT_NE NULL), maps npages anonymous private pages and fills them with ptr[i] = i; it maps them exclusively for the device with HMM_DMIRROR_EXCLUSIVE (ASSERT_EQ 0 and cpages == npages) and asserts that the device mirror holds i. It then faults the pages back by reading and incrementing each entry in system memory (asserting the old value i), asserts every entry is now i + 1, asserts that HMM_DMIRROR_CHECK_EXCLUSIVE returns 0 (the device's exclusive access has been revoked) and frees the buffer with hmm_buffer_free. A failed ASSERT_* runs the harness teardown and aborts the test process (it does not return from the body), so the buffer is not freed on that path.
note: reviewer (round15) right: a failed ASSERT_* calls __bail, which runs the teardown and abort()s (kselftest_harness.h:962-972), it does not return early from the body. Named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function).

It forks (a failed fork fails ASSERT_EQ(pid, 0)). The child increments every entry asserting the old value i, asserts every entry is i + 1 and calls _exit(0) without running the test teardown; if one of its assertions fails, the harness aborts the child. The parent does the same increment-and-verify on its own copy, then waits for the child (ASSERT_EQ(waitpid, pid)), asserts that it exited normally (WIFEXITED) with status 0, and frees the buffer. A failed ASSERT_* in the parent runs the harness teardown and aborts the test process (it does not return from the body), so the buffer is not freed on that path.
